title: quercus robur subsp. estremadurensis
intro: Quercus robur subsp. estremadurensis, commonly known as the Spanish oak, is a subspecies of the pedunculate oak tree native to southwestern Europe and western Asia. This plant is valued for its medicinal properties, including its potential to lower cholesterol levels, improve cardiovascular health, and boost the immune system. The therapeutic actions of Quercus robur subsp. estremadurensis are attributed to its ability to act as an anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and astringent, which may help alleviate symptoms of various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are believed to contribute to its health benefits.
